method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **CAP is a clinical diagnosis and is most often viral.**
claims.source_text: Community acquired pneumonia (CAP) can be diagnosed clinically and is most often due to viruses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinical definition:** fever, cough and tachypnoea at rest, plus retractions in younger children.
claims.source_text: Pneumonia can be defined clinically as the presence of fever, cough and tachypnoea at rest (and retractions in younger children)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Complicated pneumonia** means a complication such as parapneumonic effusion, empyema, lung abscess or necrotising pneumonia.
claims.source_text: “Complicated pneumonia” occurs when there is a complication such as parapneumonic effusion, empyema, lung abscess or necrotising pneumonia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Absent breath sounds with a dull percussion note suggest a pleural effusion.**
claims.source_text: Absent breath sounds and a dull percussion note suggest a pleural effusion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider severe pneumonia** when pneumonia features come with any of: severe respiratory distress · marked tachycardia · altered mental state · SpO2 <80% or needing respiratory support (e.g. CPAP, HFNP) · complicated pneumonia.
claims.source_text: Severe pneumonia should be considered if there are clinical features of pneumonia and one or more of: Severe respiratory distress Marked tachycardia Altered mental state SpO2 <80% or requiring respiratory support (eg CPAP, HFNP) Complicated pneumonia (see parapneumonic effusion)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider sepsis in severe pneumonia.** Infants under 1 month: use the seriously unwell neonate and sepsis guidelines instead.
claims.source_text: Consider sepsis in children with severe pneumonia … For infants <1 month of age see Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant and Sepsis guidelines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No routine chest X-ray, blood tests or microbiology** — especially in mild disease managed as an outpatient.
claims.source_text: Chest X-Ray, blood tests and microbiological investigations are not recommended for routine use in the diagnosis and management of CAP … Investigations, including chest X-Ray (CXR), are not recommended routinely for CAP, particularly in those with mild disease who are expected to be managed as an outpatient
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CXR when severe or complicated pneumonia is suspected.** Consider repeating it if the child deteriorates or fails to improve after 48–72 hours of appropriate antibiotics.
claims.source_text: Recommended when severe or complicated pneumonia is suspected … Consider repeating if the child deteriorates at any time or fails to clinically improve after 48-72 hours of appropriate antibiotic therapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No follow-up CXR** after uncomplicated pneumonia or a small effusion with uneventful recovery. **Follow-up CXR at 6 weeks** for complicated pneumonia, recurrent pneumonia in the same lobe, or initial suspicion of a chest mass, anatomical abnormality or foreign body.
claims.source_text: Follow-up CXR is not required for those who have uncomplicated pneumonia or small parapneumonic effusion and recover uneventfully … Follow-up CXR is recommended after 6 weeks for: complicated pneumonia recurrent pneumonia involving the same lobe or if initial suspicion of a chest mass, anatomical abnormality or foreign body
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe or complicated pneumonia:** UEC if on IV fluids · FBE and blood film · blood culture · influenza PCR · COVID-19 testing per local criteria.
claims.source_text: Severe or complicated pneumonia UEC for children receiving intravenous fluids FBE and blood film Microbiological investigations Blood culture Influenza PCR (nasal swab or aspirate) COVID-19 testing (as per local testing criteria)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not test for other viruses or atypical pathogens**: it will not change management, and atypical testing cannot separate infection from carriage.
claims.source_text: Testing for other viral pathogens will not change management … Testing for atypical pathogens is unhelpful as it does not differentiate infection from asymptomatic carriage
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CRP and procalcitonin cannot distinguish viral from bacterial cause, nor indicate severity.**
claims.source_text: Acute phase reactants (including CRP and procalcitonin) cannot distinguish between a viral or bacterial cause nor indicate severity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admit** children needing supplemental oxygen, NG or IV hydration, or with moderate to severe work of breathing.
claims.source_text: Admission to hospital is required for children who require supplemental O2, hydration support with NG or IV fluids, or moderate to severe work of breathing
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give oxygen if saturations are below 90%.**
claims.source_text: Provide supplemental oxygen if saturations are <90%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Limit NG or IV maintenance fluids to 2/3 of calculated requirement** to avoid fluid overload, with regular review of fluid status.
claims.source_text: If giving NG or IV maintenance fluids, limit fluids to 2/3 of the child’s calculated fluid requirement to avoid fluid overload, with regular clinical review of fluid status
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-severe pneumonia: high-dose oral amoxicillin, even for inpatients** — as effective as IV benzylpenicillin. Most children, including hospitalised children, can be managed orally.
claims.source_text: For non-severe pneumonia, high dose oral amoxicillin is recommended, even for inpatient use … High dose oral amoxicillin is as effective as IV benzylpenicillin … Most children, including hospitalised children, can be managed with oral antibiotics
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow local susceptibility guidance** where it differs.
claims.source_text: Antimicrobial recommendations may vary according to local antimicrobial susceptibility patterns; please refer to local guidelines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reported penicillin allergy:** assess severity using Therapeutic Guidelines and the RCH allergy prescribing guidance.
claims.source_text: Refer to Therapeutic Guidelines and Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy for guidance on assessing severity of allergy and appropriate antimicrobial options
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immediate or severe penicillin hypersensitivity, oral:** doxycycline 50 mg (<26 kg), 75 mg (26–35 kg) or 100 mg (>35 kg) twice daily, **or** azithromycin 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg) once daily.
claims.source_text: For immediate and/or severe penicillin hypersensitivity, non-beta-lactam antibiotic alternatives for CAP include Oral Doxycycline 50 mg (<26 kg), 75 mg (26-35 kg), 100 mg (>35 kg) oral BD Azithromycin 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg) oral daily
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immediate or severe penicillin hypersensitivity, IV:** ciprofloxacin 10 mg/kg (max 400 mg) IV 12-hourly **plus** vancomycin IV per local protocol.
claims.source_text: Intravenous Ciprofloxacin 10 mg/kg (max 400 mg) IV 12 hourly PLUS Vancomycin IV (see local hospital protocol for doses)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mycoplasma:** no proven benefit from treatment; it may be considered in severe pneumonia not responding to treatment.
claims.source_text: There is no proven benefit from treatment of Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia but it may be considered in severe pneumonia not responding to treatment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with the paediatric team** when the child meets admission criteria or outpatient therapy fails.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Child fulfills criteria for hospital admission Outpatient therapy fails
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for severe or complicated pneumonia, comorbidities (cardiac, chronic respiratory, immune deficiency or suppression), or care beyond the local hospital's comfort.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Severe or complicated pneumonia Comorbidities such as cardiac disease, chronic respiratory disease, immune deficiency or suppression are present Child requiring care above the level of comfort of the local hospital
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when oxygenation and oral intake are adequate.** **Outpatients need medical review in 24–48 hours.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Child is maintaining adequate oxygenation and oral intake … Note: children managed as outpatients should have medical review in 24–48 hrs
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired pneumonia' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_pneumonia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
